„Starzyński” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; autorska premiera musicalowa Teatru Syrena). VERIFIED FACTS about this production — the synopsis must not contradict any of them: (1) The action is the evening, night and morning of 26 and 27 October 1939 — never 1941. Warsaw has capitulated and the German occupation has closed in; these are Starzynski's last hours in the city hall. (2) Official atmosphere: battered Warsaw, boundless helplessness, remorse, sadness and moral dilemmas; outside are ruins, autumn, the approaching Zaduszki (All Souls') and darkness; ghosts crawl out of memories and dream mixes with waking. It ends at the threshold of his arrest. (3) The production uses fragments of Adam Mickiewicz's 'Dziady', quotations from Starzynski's own speeches, and Ludwika Nitschowa's words from Polish Radio reportage; it is inspired by Grzegorz Piatek's biography 'Starzynski. Prezydent z pomnika'. (4) Do NOT give anyone a profession the sources do not state (Wladyslaw Studnicki was a political writer, not a critic). Stanislaw Lorentz was director of the Muzeum Narodowe.
